The '''Golden Globe Award for Best Actress in a Motion Picture – Drama''' is a [[Golden Globe Awards|Golden Globe Award]] that was first awarded by the [[Hollywood Foreign Press Association]] as a separate category in 1951. Previously, there was a single award for "Best Actress in a Motion Picture", but the splitting allowed for recognition of it and the [[Golden Globe Award for Best Actress – Motion Picture Comedy or Musical|Best Actress – Comedy or Musical]].

The formal title has varied since its inception. In 2005, it was officially called "'''Best Performance by an Actress in a Motion Picture – Drama'''". As of 2013, the wording is "Best Actress in a Motion Picture – Drama".

==Firsts==
* [[Anouk Aimée]] became the first actress to win for a foreign language/non-English language performance in [[24th Golden Globe Awards|1967]].
* [[Whoopi Goldberg]] became the first actress of African descent to win in [[43rd Golden Globe Awards|1986]].
* [[Marlee Matlin]] became the first deaf actress to win in [[44th Golden Globe Awards|1987]].
* [[Jodie Foster]], [[Shirley MacLaine]], and [[Sigourney Weaver]] became the only actresses ever to win Golden Globes in a three-way tie in [[45th Golden Globe Awards|1988]].
* [[Lily Gladstone]] became the first actress of Native American heritage to win in [[81st Golden Globe Awards|2024]].
* [[Fernanda Torres]] became the first Latina as well as the first Brazilian actress to win in [[82nd Golden Globe Awards|2025]]. Coincidentally, she is the daughter of actress [[Fernanda Montenegro]], who was the first Brazilian actress to be nominated for the award in [[56th Golden Globe Awards|1999]] with her role in [[Central Station (film)|''Central Station'']].
